sentences.en: And so, Tom, what happens next?
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: So Innocent III, the great pope, perhaps the most powerful pope who has ever ruled, he's furious and he blames Raymond and sees that Raymond of Toulouse is in associate,
sentences.zh: 英诺森三世，那位伟大的教皇，也许是有史以来最有权势的教皇，他勃然大怒，他指责雷蒙德，认为图卢兹的雷蒙德是同谋，

sentences.en: you know, he's in the clutches of all these heretics that he thinks are teeming everywhere in the region.
sentences.zh: 他认为雷蒙德被该地区到处泛滥的异端分子所控制。

sentences.en: So he wants the heresy cleaned up.
sentences.zh: 所以他想要彻底清除这些异端。

sentences.en: And so he does what he's been doing for several years.
sentences.zh: 于是他做了他几年来一直在做的事情。

sentences.en: And he turns to the king of France, Philippe Augustus II, who is distracted.
sentences.zh: 他转向法国国王腓力二世·奥古斯都，但国王正分身乏术。

sentences.en: He's facing invasion by John, the king of England.
sentences.zh: 他正面临英国国王约翰的入侵。

sentences.en: He's got the Holy Roman Emperor as well.
sentences.zh: 他还要应对神圣罗马帝国皇帝。

sentences.en: And he can't be bothered.
sentences.zh: 他根本无暇顾及。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to get distracted with all this nonsense down in the south.
sentences.zh: 他不想被南方这些乱七八糟的事情分心。

sentences.en: And so he refuses.
sentences.zh: 所以他拒绝了。

sentences.en: And Innocent, he's had enough.
sentences.zh: 英诺森受够了。

sentences.en: If the king won't go, then Innocent is going to conjure up his own army.
sentences.zh: 如果国王不去，那么英诺森就要召集他自己的军队。

sentences.en: And he does it in the way that popes have been conjuring up armies to fight against the enemies
sentences.zh: 他采取了教皇自11世纪末以来召集军队对抗基督敌人的一贯方式，

sentences.en: of Christ since the end of the 11th century, which is to summon them to an armed pilgrimage.
sentences.zh: 即召集他们进行武装朝圣。

sentences.en: Now, we know these armed pilgrimages as crusades, but this is a word that doesn't start to be used until this period.
sentences.zh: 现在我们称这些武装朝圣为十字军东征，但这个词直到这一时期才开始使用。

sentences.en: And it derives from the idea that you sign yourself with the cross.
sentences.zh: 它源于你在身上画十字的观念。

sentences.en: So, cruci signati.
sentences.zh: 也就是“十字标记者”。

sentences.en: And preachers go out throughout the winter of 1208 and 1209, summoning men from a cross, not just France, but the whole of Christendom, to take up the cross.
sentences.zh: 传教士们在1208年和1209年的整个冬天四处奔走，号召人们不仅是从法国，而是从整个基督教世界出发，背起十字架。

sentences.en: So, a preacher says,
sentences.zh: 所以，一位传教士说：

sentences.en: The cross that is fixed to your coats with a soft thread was fixed to Christ's flesh with iron nails.
sentences.zh: “那用细线缝在你们外套上的十字架，曾是用铁钉钉在基督的肉体上的。”

sentences.en: In other words, that by putting on the cross, in some way they are imitating ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，通过戴上十字架，他们在某种程度上是在模仿基督。

sentences.en: And that this armed pilgrimage offers warriors the chance to live as Christ lived.
sentences.zh: 这种武装朝圣为战士们提供了像基督那样生活的机会。

sentences.en: So, that the warfare, the slaughter that they will bring is sanctified, it's holy, it's doing God's purpose, and it's emulating ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们带来的战争和屠杀是神圣的，是上帝的旨意，是在效仿基督。

sentences.en: And Peg in his book describes this as an absolutely fateful moment, that it's the merging, he says, of a century or more of Latin Christian thought on heresy and holy war.
sentences.zh: 佩克在他的书中将其描述为一个绝对决定性的时刻，他说这是拉丁基督教关于异端和圣战一个多世纪思想的融合。

sentences.en: So, you know, these are traditions, the idea of holy war, the idea that there are heretics everywhere.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些传统，圣战的观念，到处都是异端的观念，

sentences.en: These are traditions that have kind of been emerged from the great papal revolution of the 11th century, and they've been moving in parallel throughout the 12th century.
sentences.zh: 这些传统源于11世纪伟大的教皇革命，并在整个12世纪平行发展。

sentences.en: And now, under Innocent III, they're being joined.
sentences.zh: 现在，在英诺森三世的领导下，它们汇合了。

sentences.en: And, you know, this is an incredibly fateful moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极其关键的时刻。

sentences.en: And Innocent sees it as potentially apocalyptic, that if heresy is not destroyed, then, you know,
sentences.zh: 英诺森将其视为潜在的末日，如果异端不被消灭，那么，

sentences.en: it is more dangerous than, say, the Saracens, because it's a sickness within the body of Christendom itself.
sentences.zh: 它比撒拉逊人更危险，因为它本身就是基督教躯体内部的一种疾病。

sentences.en: And is this, Tom, the first great example of this idea of fighting a holy war against the enemy within?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这是对抗内部敌人进行圣战这一观念的第一个伟大例子吗？

sentences.en: I mean, that's something we're so familiar with now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这在我们现在看来太熟悉了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, the real enemies are within your house.
sentences.zh: 真正的敌人就在你的屋檐下。

sentences.en: You know, they're not the Muslims or whoever it might be.
sentences.zh: 他们不是穆斯林或其他什么人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They are other Christians.
sentences.zh: 他们是其他的基督徒。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And so, that is why the heretics are so dangerous, is that, you know, if you allow them to live, then you might become a heretic.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是为什么异端如此危险，因为如果你让他们活着，你自己也可能变成异端。

sentences.en: It's kind of like a zombie plague.
sentences.zh: 这有点像僵尸瘟疫。

sentences.en: You know, if you allow the zombies to spread, then you yourself will become a zombie.
sentences.zh: 如果你任由僵尸蔓延，你自己也会变成僵尸。

sentences.en: The real enemies are not the capitalists.

sentences.zh: 而是托洛茨基分子之类的。

sentences.en: That's what it foreshadows, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这正是它所预示的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是这样。

sentences.en: And in the episode we did on the Nazis, we were talking about how anti-Semites see the
sentences.zh: 在我们关于纳粹的那一集中，我们谈到了反犹主义者如何将犹太人视为一种疾病。

sentences.en: Jews as a kind of disease.

sentences.zh: 英诺森三世看待异端的方式也差不多。

sentences.en: And that's pretty much what Innocent III is seeing heretics as.
sentences.zh: 他认为除非消灭异端，否则他们的感染就会蔓延并腐蚀整个基督教躯体。

sentences.en: And he feels that unless the heretics are destroyed, then their infection will spread and corrupt the entire body of Christendom.
sentences.zh: 教会存在的一切目的，即引导基督徒归向上帝，都岌岌可危。

sentences.en: And everything that the church exists to do to bring the Christian people to God is in the balance.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，赌注再高不过了。

sentences.zh: 这是一场具有宇宙共鸣的战争。

sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: gets killed.
sentences.zh: 于是，他被带过街道。

sentences.zh: 基督曾受鞭笞，并被披上一件粗袍。

sentences.en: And then he is accepted back into the fold of the church.
sentences.zh: 天哪，是的。

sentences.zh: 是的，但你必须做你必须做的事。

sentences.zh: 而该地区管理基督徒生活节奏的结构，在那些坚持这些结构的人看来，比十字军的结构要神圣得多，

sentences.en: that the structures that govern the rhythms of Christian life in this region are seen by those who cleave to them as much holier,
sentences.zh: 我认为毫无疑问，在这场战争的过程中，正如战争总是会发生的那样，它加深了分裂感。

sentences.en: And I think that perhaps we should look at that later on when we look at what happens when the war is over,
sentences.zh: 我想也许我们以后在审视战争结束后会发生什么时，应该看看这一点，

sentences.en: and the degree to which this heresy, if you want to call that, survives and endures and transforMs.

sentences.en: Because one of the aspects of this that is horrifying and meant to be horrifying is that the burning of heretics is consciously offered up as a kind of holocaust,
sentences.zh: 因为这其中有一个令人毛骨悚然且旨在令人毛骨悚然的方面，那就是焚烧异端分子被刻意当作一种“大屠杀”来献祭，

sentences.zh: 作为献给主的燔祭。

sentences.en: You know, this is meant to be seen as something that is kind of simultaneously horrible and joyous.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这被视为一种既恐怖又令人愉悦的事情。

sentences.en: And that, I think, is what is so unsettling and shocking about the whole process, and was clearly unsettling to contemporaries as well.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这正是整个过程中最令人不安和震惊的地方，显然当时的人们也感到非常不安。

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.en: And that burning in Casanoi is merely the precursor for the most famous and notorious holocaust of the lot,
sentences.zh: 而卡萨诺伊的那场焚烧，仅仅是这一系列中最著名、最臭名昭著的大屠杀的前奏，

sentences.en: which is the great town of Béziers, which is one of the two cities that are under the certainty of the vicomte of Béziers and Carcassonne.
sentences.zh: 那就是贝济耶大屠杀，它是贝济耶和卡尔卡松子爵管辖下的两座城市之一。

sentences.en: One listeners from the previous episode will remember that, you know, these are the great rivals of the Counts of Toulouse.
sentences.zh: 听过上一集的听众会记得，你知道，这些是图卢兹伯爵的劲敌。

sentences.en: And the vicomte of Béziers and Carcassonne in this period is a guy called Raymond Roger, and he is both the nephew and the rival of Raymond, the Count of Toulouse.
sentences.zh: 当时贝济耶和卡尔卡松的子爵是一个叫雷蒙·罗杰的人，他既是图卢兹伯爵雷蒙的侄子，也是他的竞争对手。

sentences.en: So they kind of, you know, they're related, but they hate each other in the best traditions of medieval lords.
sentences.zh: 所以他们算是亲戚，但按照中世纪领主的优良传统，他们彼此仇视。

sentences.en: And this is why Raymond VI, who has, you know, repented, recanted, been welcomed back into the world of the church and become a crusader,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么雷蒙六世——他已经忏悔、放弃异端、重新被教会世界接纳并成为了一名十字军战士——

sentences.en: when he approaches Arnold Amalrec, the abbot of Citeau, who is serving as the papal representative with this huge army, he turns up and he says, I think you should go to Béziers.
sentences.zh: 当他找到担任教皇代表、统领这支庞大军队的西多会修道院院长阿诺德·阿马尔里克时，他出现并说，我认为你应该去贝济耶。

sentences.en: So, in other words, target the city of his greatest rival.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，就是去攻击他最大对手的城市。

sentences.en: And Raymond Roger, who's only 24 and hasn't really been keeping track of what's been going on,
sentences.zh: 而年仅24岁、对局势并不太了解的雷蒙·罗杰，

sentences.en: is suddenly informed that the greatest Christian army ever, as it's being described, is, you know, is coming towards him.
sentences.zh: 突然接到消息说，正如人们所描述的那样，史上最伟大的基督教军队正向他逼近。

sentences.en: He summons all the people of Béziers to a meeting and he says, guys, you're on your own.
sentences.zh: 他召集了贝济耶的所有人开会，并对他们说，伙计们，你们只能靠自己了。

sentences.en: And then he scrams and heads off and kind of hunkers down in Carcassonne.
sentences.zh: 然后他溜之大吉，躲进了卡尔卡松。

sentences.en: And the people in Béziers think, oh, God.
sentences.zh: 贝济耶的人民心想，天哪。

sentences.en: And the whole story is tragic and comic in equal measure, because the crusading army camps down in front of the walls of Béziers.
sentences.zh: 整个故事既悲剧又滑稽，因为十字军大军在贝济耶城墙外扎营。

sentences.en: Béziers has very, very strong fortifications.
sentences.zh: 贝济耶拥有非常、非常坚固的防御工事。

sentences.en: The people in Béziers think they're absolutely fine.
sentences.zh: 贝济耶的人民认为他们绝对安全。

sentences.en: Nothing, you know, they're not going to be stormed.
sentences.zh: 没什么，你知道，他们不会被攻破的。

sentences.en: And kind of various lads, they go out onto the bridge and they start kind of jeering at the crusaders.
sentences.zh: 于是各种小伙子跑到桥上，开始嘲笑十字军。

sentences.en: And saying, you know, you're never going to get us and kind of, you know, running out, sneering at them and then running back in.
sentences.zh: 说，你知道，你们永远抓不到我们，然后跑出去，对他们冷嘲热讽，再跑回来。

sentences.en: And there's a whole gang of lads who are accompanying the crusaders.
sentences.zh: 还有一大帮随军的年轻人。

sentences.en: So they are described as ribald boys.
sentences.zh: 他们被称为“粗俗的男孩”。

sentences.en: But I suppose, you know, if you're in Liverpool, you might call them scallies, I guess.
sentences.zh: 但我想，如果你在利物浦，你可能会叫他们“小混混”，我想是这样。

sentences.en: It's that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 就是那种感觉。

sentences.en: You know, they're kind of lads who are camp followers.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们是那种随军的混混。

sentences.en: But, you know, they've got a bit of...
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，他们有点……

sentences.en: They fancy a fight.
sentences.zh: 他们想打一架。

sentences.en: They fancy a fight.
sentences.zh: 他们想打一架。

sentences.en: And basically, they're not having this stuff that, you know, all the lads in Béziers.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们受不了贝济耶那些小伙子的挑衅。

sentences.en: So they follow it and they get into a punch-up.
sentences.zh: 所以他们跟了上去，打了起来。

sentences.zh: 接着冲突升级，他们开始蜂拥而上。

sentences.en: And before they know it, they've captured Béziers.
sentences.zh: 还没等他们反应过来，他们就已经占领了贝济耶。

sentences.en: And all the knights kind of look up and go, oh!
sentences.zh: 所有的骑士抬头一看，噢！

sentences.en: And so they pile in and the slaughter proceeds.
sentences.zh: 于是他们一拥而上，屠杀开始了。

sentences.zh: 所以佩格在《最神圣的战争》中写道，随着血流顺着街道流下并冲刷过桥梁，天空渐渐变暗。

sentences.en: Sounds like one of my children's books, Tom.
sentences.zh: 听起来像我孩子读的童书，汤姆。

sentences.zh: 据统计有7000人在那里被焚烧。

sentences.zh: 有一位名叫劳伦斯·马文的学者写过一本书，他关注的重点不是宗教层面，而是军事层面。

sentences.en: And he points out that this figure couldn't possibly be true because, as many observers, including myself, have concluded,
sentences.zh: 他指出这个数字不可能属实，因为正如包括我在内的许多观察家所总结的那样，

sentences.en: the church is simply not large enough to accommodate that many people.
sentences.zh: 教堂根本容纳不下那么多人。

sentences.en: So that's an apt point.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个中肯的观点。

sentences.en: He's a fun-hating historian, I think, is the expression.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是所谓的“扫兴的历史学家”。

sentences.en: But the point is that the incineration encourages these kind of stories because it's designed to be absolutely shocking.
sentences.zh: 但重点是，这种焚烧助长了这类故事，因为它的设计目的就是为了绝对的震撼。

sentences.en: You know, this is a burnt offering to the Lord, and the news of it reverberates across Christendom.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是献给主的燔祭，其消息传遍了整个基督教世界。

sentences.en: It's an absolutely pointed display of divine vengeance.
sentences.zh: 这是一种绝对尖锐的神圣复仇展示。

sentences.en: That's what it's meant to be.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的本意。

sentences.en: And a decade after it, perhaps the most famous saying that emerges from the Abigensian Crusade is attributed to Arnold Amelric, who is the papal envoy.
sentences.zh: 十年后，阿尔比十字军中最著名的名言被归功于教皇特使阿诺德·阿马尔里克。

sentences.en: And when the crusaders bursting into Bézier, and they can't distinguish between heretics and non-heretics, and one of them asks Amelric, well, you know, what do we do?
sentences.zh: 当十字军冲进贝济耶，无法区分异端和非异端时，其中一人问阿马尔里克，好吧，我们该怎么办？

sentences.en: How can we tell them apart?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么区分他们？

sentences.en: And the abbot replies, kill them.
sentences.zh: 修道院院长回答说，杀光他们。

sentences.en: Truly, God will know his enemy.
sentences.zh: 上帝自会辨认出他的敌人。

sentences.en: And whether he says that or not, it gets taken up and repeated because it articulates something very, very important,
sentences.zh: 无论他是否真的说过这句话，它都被采纳并流传开来，因为它阐明了一个非常、非常重要的观点，

sentences.en: that the need to scour the region of heresy is more important than allowing the innocent to survive.
sentences.zh: 即清除该地区的异端比让无辜者幸存更重要。

sentences.en: So better 10 innocent men are killed than one guilty man go free, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，宁可错杀一千无辜，不可放过一个罪人。

sentences.en: And so Amelric writes to the Pope, and he says that in Bézier, where thousands of people have been slaughtered or incinerated, he says, divine vengeance raged marvelously.
sentences.zh: 于是阿马尔里克写信给教皇，他说在贝济耶，成千上万的人被屠杀或焚烧，他说，神圣的复仇奇迹般地爆发了。

sentences.en: Crikey.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.zh: 这可不是“打左脸给右脸”，对吧？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: But, you know, but it is seen as the crusaders feel that they are imitating Christ in doing this, that this is what Christ wants, that this is what he would do.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，十字军确实认为他们在模仿基督，认为这是基督想要的，是基督会做的事。

sentences.en: So it's very, it's kind of very sanguinary and weird and terrifying.
sentences.zh: 所以这非常血腥、怪异且令人恐惧。

sentences.en: And understandably, everyone in Carcassonne, you know, I mean, they're, again, to use the technical term, crapping themselves.
sentences.zh: 可以理解的是，卡尔卡松的所有人，你知道，用专业术语来说，都吓尿了。

sentences.en: And the crusaders put Carcassonne under siege for three weeks.
sentences.zh: 十字军对卡尔卡松进行了为期三周的围攻。

sentences.en: After this period, Raymond Roger decides, I've had enough, and he opens negotiations.
sentences.zh: 这段时间过后，雷蒙·罗杰决定，我受够了，于是他开启了谈判。

sentences.en: Inhabitants are allowed to leave wearing only their shirts, and so they do so, all of them.

sentences.zh: 确实没有裤子。

sentences.zh: 该地区的人以穿着紧身亮黄色绑腿而闻名。

sentences.en: So perhaps they're wearing those, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 所以也许他们穿着那个，我不知道。

sentences.en: Ungodly, Tom.
sentences.zh: 真是不敬虔，汤姆。

sentences.en: Very ungodly.
sentences.zh: 非常不敬虔。

sentences.zh: 但可怜的雷蒙·罗杰本人却被俘虏了，尽管他曾得到安全通行的承诺。

sentences.en: He's chained up, and he dies three months later.
sentences.zh: 他被锁起来，三个月后去世了。

sentences.en: So he is out of the way.
sentences.zh: 所以他出局了。

sentences.zh: 现在的问题是，谁将成为贝济耶和卡尔卡松的新领主？

sentences.en: And there are kind of various lords from the north of France who have turned up, and they all think, actually, you know, this is a hiding for nothing.
sentences.zh: 来自法国北部的几位领主出现了，他们都认为，说实话，这根本没好处。

sentences.en: Because the crusaders are, you know, their vow is to fight for 40 days, and the 40 days are up.
sentences.zh: 因为十字军的誓言是战斗40天，而40天期限已到。

sentences.en: And so the likelihood is, is that large numbers are going to go away.
sentences.zh: 所以很有可能，大批人马会离开。

sentences.en: So whoever is left in Bézier and Carcassonne is going to be surrounded by a very hostile population, not have many men.
sentences.zh: 因此，无论谁留在贝济耶和卡尔卡松，都将被敌对的人群包围，且没有多少兵力。

sentences.en: So they're all a bit nervous, so they say no.
sentences.zh: 所以他们都很紧张，于是他们拒绝了。

sentences.zh: 他是一位40多岁的人。

sentences.en: And when the vast mass of the crusaders leave after the capture of Carcassonne, he's left with perhaps a hundred knights, a few more.

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不是，你知道，人数非常、非常少。

sentences.en: And then in the winter,
sentences.zh: 然后在冬天，

sentences.en: And it's absolutely hideous.

sentences.zh: 是的，那是一个非常、非常坚不可摧的地方。

sentences.en: And one of the crusaders says, well, what's all this about?
sentences.zh: 其中一个十字军说，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: We want to burn them.
sentences.zh: 我们想烧死他们。

sentences.en: And Amorick says, don't worry, I can guarantee you that it'll be fine, because loads of them will not accept the pardon.
sentences.zh: 阿马尔里克说，别担心，我保证没问题，因为他们中很多人不会接受赦免。

sentences.en: And so 140 of the people of Minerve are burned.
sentences.zh: 于是140名米内尔夫的居民被烧死。

sentences.en: And it is reported that they were so hardened in their wickedness that they hurled themselves into the flames of their own accord.
sentences.zh: 据报道，他们顽固不化，自愿投身火海。

sentences.en: So, again, this idea of the heretics willingly embracing the flame.
sentences.zh: 所以，再次强调，这种异端分子自愿拥抱火焰的想法。

sentences.en: And you get a kind of detail that's almost kind of reminiscent of the episode that we did on the Holocaust,
sentences.zh: 你得到了一种细节，几乎让人想起我们做过的那期关于大屠杀的节目，

sentences.en: that afterwards the corpses have to be buried in mud because the stench of charred flesh is so revolting that crusaders who've just arrived just keep retching and vomiting.
sentences.zh: 事后尸体必须埋在泥里，因为烧焦的肉味太令人作呕，以至于刚到的十字军不停地干呕和呕吐。

sentences.en: 1211, a place called Lavar is captured, 400 heretics are burned alive.
sentences.zh: 1211年，一个叫拉瓦尔的地方被攻占，400名异端分子被活活烧死。

sentences.en: And again, this is done with kind of a sense of joy.
sentences.zh: 同样，这也是带着一种喜悦感完成的。

sentences.en: So it's cum ingenti gaudio, the phrase is the Latin phrase, with great joy.
sentences.zh: 所以是“cum ingenti gaudio”，这是拉丁语短语，意为“带着巨大的喜悦”。

sentences.en: And at Lavar, the lady of the city, who is not herself a heretic, but is accused of having been favorable to the heretics,
sentences.zh: 在拉瓦尔，那位城市的女主人，她本人不是异端，但被指控对异端分子表示同情，

sentences.en: she's thrown down a well and the crusader's hull rocks onto her until she's crushed.
sentences.zh: 她被扔进了一口井里，十字军把石头扔在她身上，直到她被压死。

sentences.en: You've used the word heretics a lot to describe the people who are being executed or the people who are being accused.
sentences.zh: 你用了“异端”这个词很多次来描述那些被处决或被指控的人。

sentences.en: And is it fair to say this is irrespective of their heretics is just the label that is being pinned on them because they are the local people of the long dock who are on the wrong side?
sentences.zh: 公平地说，这是否与他们是否真的是异端无关，这只是贴在他们身上的标签，因为他们是朗格多克当地人，站在了错误的一边？

sentences.en: No, I think they are people who do hold opinions that would be defined.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为他们确实持有会被定义为异端的观点。

sentences.en: Oh, they do hold opinions, right.
sentences.zh: 噢，他们确实持有观点，对吧。

sentences.en: I think so, yes.
sentences.zh: 我想是的，没错。

sentences.en: And we'll talk about exactly how these opinions may have evolved over the course of the crusade in the second half when we look at what happens in the aftermath of the war.
sentences.zh: 我们将在下半部分讨论这些观点在十字军东征过程中是如何演变的，届时我们将审视战争结束后发生了什么。

sentences.en: But just to continue with the kind of the sense of the horrors of it, you have, as well as Holocaust, you have calculated atrocities.
sentences.zh: 但为了继续讲述那种恐怖感，除了大屠杀，还有蓄意的暴行。

sentences.en: So, you know, garrisons will be captured.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，驻军会被俘虏。

sentences.en: De Montfort will cut off, will mutilate them, cut off the noses, you know, gouge out the eyes.
sentences.zh: 德·孟福尔会切断、残害他们，割掉鼻子，你知道，挖出眼睛。

sentences.en: And it's happening the other way around as well.
sentences.zh: 反过来也是如此。

sentences.en: So if, I don't know, monks have been captured, they'll be murdered.
sentences.zh: 如果，我不知道，僧侣被俘虏，他们会被谋杀。

sentences.en: De Montfort's knights, if they get captured, there's a kind of a horrible story about them.
sentences.zh: 德·孟福尔的骑士如果被俘，有一个关于他们的可怕故事。

sentences.en: You know, they have their eyes gouged out and they're sent out into the winter to stumble their way back to Carcassonne.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们的眼睛被挖出来，然后被送进冬天，跌跌撞撞地走回卡尔卡松。

sentences.en: And occasionally there are battles and campaigns in the open.
sentences.zh: 偶尔也会有公开的战斗和战役。

sentences.en: And one of them is against the king of Aragon, who is coming to try and get rid of Simon de Montfort and lay claim to this region himself.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是针对阿拉贡国王，他前来试图除掉西蒙·德·孟福尔，并亲自宣称对该地区的主权。

sentences.en: And he gets killed in a great battle at a place called Muret.
sentences.zh: 他在穆雷的一场大战中被杀。

sentences.en: So this sense of slaughter and horror is kind of escalating.
sentences.zh: 所以这种屠杀和恐怖感在某种程度上不断升级。

sentences.en: But by and large, people are across Christendom are seeing it as a kind of salutary demonstration of the power of ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，整个基督教世界的人们将其视为一种对基督力量的有益展示。

sentences.en: So Peg begins his book, A Most Holy War, with this incredible description of one of the first ghosts to appear from purgatory.
sentences.zh: 佩格在他的著作《最神圣的战争》开头，描述了第一批从炼狱中出现的鬼魂之一，令人难以置信。

sentences.en: It's a small boy who appears to a small girl.
sentences.zh: 那是一个出现在一个小女孩面前的小男孩。

sentences.en: And he says, he assures this girl that nothing has pleased God so much as the death and extermination of the Albigensians.
sentences.zh: 他说，他向这个女孩保证，没有什么比消灭阿尔比派教徒更让上帝高兴的了。

sentences.en: And the Albigensians is the word that's being used for the heretics of the region at Al-Bizhoa.
sentences.zh: “阿尔比派”是当时用来称呼阿尔比地区异教徒的词。

sentences.en: And so it just goes on and on like this for kind of 20 years, endless slaughter, endless burning of fields until finally in 1218,
sentences.zh: 就这样，这种状况持续了大约20年，无休止的屠杀，无休止的焚烧田野，直到1218年，

sentences.en: you get this kind of deadlock between Simon de Montfort and Raymond VI, who is holed up in Toulouse.
sentences.zh: 西蒙·德·蒙福尔和躲在图卢兹的雷蒙六世之间陷入了僵局。

sentences.en: Simon wants to capture Toulouse and he feels this will end the war.
sentences.zh: 西蒙想攻占图卢兹，他觉得这样战争就会结束。

sentences.en: And Simon vows that he will capture Toulouse within a week.
sentences.zh: 西蒙发誓要在这一周内攻下图卢兹。

sentences.en: And the following day, the ladies and the small girls of Toulouse are busy working a kind of siege engine, you know, because it's all hands to the deck.
sentences.zh: 第二天，图卢兹的妇女和女孩们正忙着操作一种攻城器械，因为每个人都得参与进来。

sentences.en: They fire it and it crashes into Simon's head and he drops dead.
sentences.zh: 她们发射了它，它砸中了西蒙的头，他当场毙命。

sentences.en: Oh, that's a nice ending.
sentences.zh: 哦，那真是个不错的结局。

sentences.en: I'm glad that he's dead, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我很高兴他死了。

sentences.en: I didn't I didn't care for him.
sentences.zh: 我一点也不喜欢他。

sentences.en: I have to say he's he's a terrifying man.
sentences.zh: 我得说，他是个可怕的人。

sentences.en: And with him gone, everything kind of falls to pieces because his son, Amory, is who inherits that, you know, Simon, Simon de Montfort,
sentences.zh: 他一死，一切都分崩离析了，因为他的儿子阿莫里继承了这一切，你知道，西蒙，西蒙·德·蒙福尔，

sentences.en: the younger Simon inherits his olden of Leicester, which is why he's able to, you know, be the founder of English democracy.
sentences.zh: 年轻的西蒙继承了他父亲的莱斯特伯爵爵位，这就是为什么他后来能成为英国民主的奠基人。

sentences.en: But Amory turns out to be absolutely useless and he can't hold it together.
sentences.zh: 但阿莫里表现得极其无能，他无法掌控局面。

sentences.en: And so the son of Philip II, the king of France, Louis, he is made of much sterner stuff.
sentences.zh: 于是法国国王腓力二世的儿子路易，他比他坚强得多。

sentences.en: He's much more of an enthusiast for for Crusade than Philip.
sentences.zh: 他比腓力更热衷于十字军东征。

sentences.en: And so in 1219, he does go down to this region and he conducts a siege of Toulouse.
sentences.zh: 所以在1219年，他确实去了那个地区，并对图卢兹进行了围攻。

sentences.en: It's just about to fall.
sentences.zh: 它几乎就要陷落了。

sentences.en: Then the 40 days are up.
sentences.zh: 然后40天的期限到了。

sentences.en: And so Louis feels that he's done his duty.
sentences.zh: 路易觉得他已经尽到了职责。

sentences.en: And so he goes back.
sentences.zh: 于是他回去了。

sentences.en: And so Toulouse survives and Raymond VI survives.
sentences.zh: 所以图卢兹幸存了下来，雷蒙六世也幸存了下来。

sentences.en: And Raymond then dies in 1222.
sentences.zh: 雷蒙随后在1222年去世。

sentences.en: And his son, inevitably called Raymond, wants to bury him in a priory in Toulouse.
sentences.zh: 他的儿子，不可避免地也叫雷蒙，想把他葬在图卢兹的一座修道院里。

sentences.en: But he can't because his dad is still excommunicated.
sentences.zh: 但他做不到，因为他父亲仍然被逐出教会。

sentences.en: And so the coffin with Raymond's body in it has to be left outside the priory church, where it is left for 200 years.
sentences.zh: 所以装着雷蒙遗体的棺材不得不被留在修道院教堂外，在那里放了200年。

sentences.en: 200 years?
Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it kind of, you know, it gets, you know, his body gets eaten by rats.
sentences.zh: 他的尸体被老鼠吃了。

sentences.en: The coffin rots away and it all just completely vanishes.
sentences.zh: 棺材腐烂了，一切都彻底消失了。

sentences.en: So it's a kind of another dimension of the horrible.
sentences.zh: 所以这是恐怖的另一个维度。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So many gothic details in this story.
sentences.zh: 这个故事里有太多哥特式的细节了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Raymond VII succeeds him.
sentences.zh: 雷蒙七世继位了。

sentences.en: He's very kind of vigorous and able, but he knows really that he's up against it.
sentences.zh: 他非常有活力和能力，但他确实知道自己面临着严峻的挑战。

sentences.en: Because by this point, Philip II's son, Louis, has become Louis VIII.
sentences.zh: 因为到这个时候，腓力二世的儿子路易已经成为了路易八世。

sentences.en: And he really, really is determined to kind of annex the whole region and bring it under, directly under French rule.
sentences.zh: 他真的非常非常决心吞并整个地区，并将其直接置于法国的统治之下。

sentences.en: So 1224, Louis VIII accepts the lands that Améry de Montfort had inherited from his father, and he takes them over.
sentences.zh: 所以1224年，路易八世接受了阿莫里·德·蒙福尔从他父亲那里继承的土地，并接管了它们。

sentences.en: So these are now kind of property of the French crown.
sentences.zh: 所以这些现在成了法国王室的财产。

sentences.en: And two years after that, in 1226, he takes the cross.
sentences.zh: 两年后的1226年，他参加了十字军。

sentences.en: He leads the crusade, the largest crusade since 1209, and he invades the Languedoc.
sentences.zh: 他领导了自1209年以来规模最大的十字军东征，并入侵了朗格多克。

sentences.en: And again, it looks as though it's all up for Raymond.
sentences.zh: 看起来雷蒙又要完了。

sentences.en: But Louis VIII falls ill, and he is taken back in a litter to Paris, and most people attribute it to dysentery.
sentences.zh: 但路易八世病倒了，他被抬回了巴黎，大多数人认为这是痢疾。

sentences.en: But there is one courtier thinks that it's because Louis VIII is very pious, that he hasn't been having enough sex.
sentences.zh: 但有一位朝臣认为，这是因为路易八世非常虔诚，他一直没有进行足够的性生活。

sentences.en: And so he introduces a courtesan into the, you know, the tent where Louis is wasting away.
sentences.zh: 于是他把一个妓女带进了路易正在消瘦的帐篷里。

sentences.en: And Louis is said to have covered his private parts and told the prostitute,
sentences.zh: 据说路易遮住了自己的私处，并对那个妓女说，

sentences.en: Madam, it shall not be.
sentences.zh: 夫人，这不可以。

sentences.en: And he dies shortly afterwards.
sentences.zh: 不久之后他就去世了。

sentences.en: Which to be fair, if he was wasting away, he's probably not in the mood.
sentences.zh: 说实话，如果他当时正在消瘦，他可能也没什么心情。

sentences.en: Quite, exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实，完全正确。

sentences.en: So 1228, Raymond VII finally kind of sues for peace.
sentences.zh: 所以1228年，雷蒙七世终于求和了。

sentences.en: You know, he says, I give up.
sentences.zh: 他说，我放弃了。

sentences.en: And 1229, peace treaty is signed in Paris, and this brings the war officially to an end.
sentences.zh: 1229年，巴黎签署了和平条约，这标志着战争正式结束。

sentences.en: And by its terms, Raymond remains the count of Toulouse, but he loses a great eastern chunk of his territory, which goes to the French crown.
sentences.zh: 根据条款，雷蒙保留了图卢兹伯爵的头衔，但他失去了东部大片领土，这些领土归了法国王室。

sentences.en: The French crown has also grabbed Bézier Carcassonne.
sentences.zh: 法国王室还夺取了贝济耶和卡尔卡松。

sentences.en: They keep that.
sentences.zh: 他们保留了这些地方。

sentences.en: Raymond's daughter, who's nine years old, a little girl called Joanne, is attributed to Louis' younger brother, a guy called Alphonse.
sentences.zh: 雷蒙九岁的女儿，一个叫琼的小女孩，被许配给了路易的弟弟，一个叫阿方斯的人。

sentences.en: And the stipulation is, is that their children will be the heirs of Raymond.
sentences.zh: 规定是，他们的孩子将成为雷蒙的继承人。

sentences.en: So they will inherit the lands of Toulouse.
sentences.zh: 所以他们将继承图卢兹的土地。

sentences.en: But the problem is, is that they don't have children.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，他们没有孩子。

sentences.en: And so when Alphonse and Joanne both die in 1271, Toulouse as well passes to the French crown.
sentences.zh: 所以当阿方斯和琼在1271年双双去世时，图卢兹也归了法国王室。

sentences.en: And so it becomes part of the fabric of the kingdom of France.
sentences.zh: 它成为了法兰西王国的一部分。

sentences.en: And the other term is that Raymond will continue to hunt out the heretics.
sentences.zh: 另一个条款是雷蒙将继续搜捕异教徒。

sentences.en: And so even though the war has ended, the war against heresy hasn't.
sentences.zh: 所以尽管战争结束了，但针对异端的战争并没有结束。

sentences.en: And I think that, you know, we should take a break.
sentences.zh: 我想我们应该休息一下。

sentences.en: And definitely when we come back, look at basically, you know, it's a question that you've been asking over again.
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，肯定会看看你一直在问的问题。

sentences.en: And I'm sure the listeners have been pondering it as well.
sentences.zh: 我相信听众们也一直在思考这个问题。

sentences.en: It's, you know, you know, if there is no heresy or no major heresy, why are they hurling themselves into the flames?
sentences.zh: 如果没有异端，或者没有主要的异端，为什么他们要投身于火焰中呢？

sentences.en: And perhaps talk about that.
sentences.zh: 也许可以谈谈这个。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: With a sudden upwelling of reverence, Robert Langdon fell to his knees.
sentences.zh: 带着突然涌起的敬畏，罗伯特·兰登跪了下来。

sentences.en: For a moment, he thought he heard Tom Holland's voice, the wisdom of the ages, whispering up from the chasms of the earth.
sentences.zh: 有一瞬间，他以为自己听到了汤姆·霍兰的声音，那是来自大地深渊的、低语着的历代智慧。

sentences.en: That's what it feels like for me, Tom, listening to you talk about the Cathars.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，听你谈论卡特里派，我就是这种感觉。

sentences.en: Those are, of course, the final lines of the Da Vinci Code.
sentences.zh: 当然，那是《达芬奇密码》的最后几行。

sentences.en: One of the great texts of 2003, of the 21st century, perhaps even of all time, said nobody ever.
sentences.zh: 2003年、21世纪，甚至是有史以来最伟大的著作之一，没人说过。

sentences.en: Well, I'm sure Dan Brown must have said that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我相信丹·布朗肯定说过。

sentences.en: I think he, I'm sure he's not an immodest man, is he?
sentences.zh: 我想他不是一个谦虚的人，对吧？

sentences.en: He might well say that other books, Angels and Demons, Inferno, are superior as he's honed his craft.
sentences.zh: 他很可能会说其他书，比如《天使与魔鬼》、《地狱》，随着他技艺的精进，更加出色。

sentences.en: So, Tom, we started with the Da Vinci Code.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，我们从《达芬奇密码》开始。

sentences.en: We've actually found our way into, I think, a much stranger and more interesting story.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上发现了一个我认为更奇怪、更有趣的故事。

sentences.en: This is the story of the Albigensian Crusade.
sentences.zh: 这就是阿尔比派十字军的故事。

sentences.en: Completely agree.
sentences.zh: 完全同意。

sentences.en: It is an extraordinary, fascinating story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非凡而迷人的故事。

sentences.en: So, we ended with the end of the war.
sentences.zh: 我们以战争的结束作为结尾。

sentences.en: The counts of Toulouse have become belittled.
sentences.zh: 图卢兹伯爵们的地位被削弱了。

sentences.en: I mean, they have less territory.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们的领土变少了。

sentences.en: Their French crown has got more territory.
sentences.zh: 法国王室获得了更多的领土。

sentences.en: So, you could look at this and say, well, this is just basically a land grab.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以这样看，这基本上就是一场土地掠夺。

sentences.en: But for the fact that you ended by saying that the counts of Toulouse were told they had to continue fighting heresy and rooting out heresy,
sentences.zh: 但你最后说图卢兹伯爵被告知必须继续打击和根除异端，

sentences.en: which suggests that it's not just a fig leaf.
sentences.zh: 这表明这不仅仅是一个借口。

sentences.en: There's something very substantial going on there.
sentences.zh: 那里正在发生一些非常实质性的事情。

sentences.en: And how is that war on heresy that this was supposed to be all about?
sentences.zh: 那么这场本应是关于打击异端的战争到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: What's been going on with that?
sentences.zh: 那方面进展如何？

sentences.en: So, I mean, right the way through, I've been saying that by the lights of the Roman Church, there are lots of people in this region who do count as heretics.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我一直说，按照罗马教会的观点，这个地区有很多人确实算作异教徒。

sentences.en: And the particular focus is this notion that there are people called boni homines, the good men, the good women,
sentences.zh: 特别关注的是一种观念，即有被称为“好人”（boni homines）的人，好男人，好女人，

sentences.en: who can attain a holiness that is equal to or greater than that of priests.
sentences.zh: 他们可以获得等同于或高于神职人员的圣洁。

sentences.en: And this is absolute anathema to the Roman Church.
sentences.zh: 这对罗马教会来说是绝对的诅咒。

sentences.en: The division between laity and priests is fundamental to it, both because they have a very elevated sense of the role of the priesthood,
sentences.zh: 平信徒和神职人员之间的划分是其根本，不仅因为他们对神职的作用有非常崇高的认识，

sentences.en: but also because it's the priests and the clerics and the scholars who are responsible for instructing the vast mass of the Christian people in Christian doctrine.
